answer: Plume-gated admission. Each period, a public verifier derives a random seed from a committed future oracle value, then assigns each new agent a slot in a crystal lattice of registration windows. An identity must register in its assigned slot; late or duplicate slots are void. Attackers cannot precompute slots before the seed reveals, so mass pre-registration fails. Each rejected attempt costs a copper-denominated fee plus forfeiture of the slot deposit, making large sybil batches linearly expensive.
